summary:
Our project is an interactive educational website designed to introduce middle school students to space exploration through the fascinating topic of objects abandoned on the Moon by NASA astronauts and missions.

The main goal of our website is to make learning about space more interesting, engaging, and enjoyable for our age group. Instead of simply reading information, users can explore different abandoned objects through an interactive game. In the game, players have to search for hidden objects. When they find an object, it introduces itself and shares information about its history and purpose. Players then complete a quiz about the object to earn and collect it. This combines exploration, learning, and testing knowledge in one experience.

Our website includes quizzes to help students remember what they learn and a game that encourages curiosity and active participation. The intended impact is to increase students' interest in space, NASA, and the history of lunar exploration.

For the technical side, we used Three.js and WebGL to create interactive 3D and holographic experiences. We also included a 50kg Lunar Liftoff Physics Simulator, an Interactive Cadet Archaeology Exam, and a Procedural Web Audio API Soundboard to make the experience more immersive.

Overall, our project combines education, gaming, physics, and interactive technology to turn learning about NASA's lunar missions into an exciting adventure for middle school students.
details:
Our project is an interactive educational website designed to make middle school students more interested in space by teaching them about objects left behind on the Moon by NASA missions. The website combines education, gaming, and interactive technology to create an exciting learning experience.

Users can explore our website, discover different objects left on the Moon, and learn about their history and purpose. We also created an interactive game in which players search for hidden objects. When a player finds an object, it introduces itself and explains what it is. The player then completes a quiz about the object to earn and collect it. This makes learning more enjoyable while testing the user's knowledge.

Our project benefits students by encouraging curiosity, improving their knowledge of space exploration, and making educational content more engaging. Our main goal is to inspire middle school students to learn more about NASA, the Moon, and the history of space exploration.

To develop our project, we used Three.js and WebGL for interactive 3D and holographic experiences. We also incorporated a 50kg Lunar Liftoff Physics Simulator, an Interactive Cadet Archaeology Exam, and a Procedural Web Audio API Soundboard to make the website more immersive and interactive.

The creative aspect of our project is that we turned learning into an adventure. Instead of presenting information through ordinary text, we allowed users to discover objects, interact with them, and earn them by answering quizzes. This makes the educational experience feel more like a game.

While developing the project, our team considered our target audience, middle school students, and focused on making the website interesting, educational, interactive, and easy to enjoy. We wanted to balance learning with entertainment so that students could gain knowledge while having fun.

Overall, our project aims to bring the history of lunar exploration to life and inspire the next generation to become curious about space and science.
